findings.title: Recovery codes stored by the user-storage provider are never consumed
findings.body: The recovery-code validation path only checks whether the submitted code is present in the deserialized list and never removes that code or updates the stored credential. Consequently, every recovery code created through this user storage remains valid indefinitely and can be replayed after a successful login, violating the one-time-use security property of recovery codes. The storage provider must atomically mark/remove the matched code on successful validation, and the integration test should authenticate with the same code twice and verify the second attempt fails.

findings.title: Federated recovery credential reconstruction drops the persisted credential identity
findings.body: `recoveryCodesModel` has a generated ID when it is persisted, but `createFromValues` is called with only the codes, creation time, and label, so the returned credential cannot retain that persisted ID. Consumers now use this reconstructed federated credential; in particular, the recovery authenticator removes an exhausted credential by the returned ID. That ID is null or a newly generated value rather than the stored credential ID, so cleanup/removal cannot reliably target the provider's credential and credential metadata has an unstable identity. Preserve the persisted ID (and other persisted metadata such as the label) when exposing the `CredentialModel` from `getCredentials`.
